## Natural history notes

A large swallowtail butterfly characterized by bright yellow wings with bold black tiger-like stripes, long hindwing tails, and blue and orange markings near the hindwing edges; some females are mostly dark instead of yellow. In Florida, the Eastern Tiger Swallowtail is found in hardwood forests, hammocks, forest edges, parks, gardens, roadsides, and wooded neighborhoods where host trees are available. Adults visit flowers for nectar, while the caterpillars feed on leaves of trees such as tuliptree, sweetbay, wild cherry, ash, and other hardwoods, resting on leaves with eyespot-like markings that help deter predators.
